newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Divisions in Indonesian minority party increase.
newsitem.headline: Divisions in Indonesian minority party increase.

text.p: Legislators loyal to the ousted leader of the Indonesian Democratic Party (PDI), Megawati Sukarnoputri, called on Friday for a rival government-backed faction to end campaigning for this month's general elections.

Supporters of Megawati have begun moving toward the other minority party permitted to contest elections, the United Development Party (PPP), and the government-backed PDI faction, headed by parliamentary deputy speaker Surjadi was fast becoming irrelevant, they said.

"The PDI under Surjadi obviously does not have any support from the public and this can be seen from the rejection made by the public and the PDI supporters led by Megawati," said a statement signed by 13 legislators which was handed over to parliamentary speaker Wahono.
"If Surjadi continues to campaign, we are afraid it will create instability. The PDI under Surjadi is not fit to participate in the election campaign.
"During each campaign organised by Surjadi, only hundreds or even tens of people attend the event and security officers outnumber campaign participants," it said.
The Christian-Nationalist PDI split into two camps after Megawati was ousted at a government-backed congress last year which replaced her with Surjadi.

Megawati's faction has been banned from contesting general elections on May 29, in which the Moslem-oriented PPP and the PDI are battling the ruling Golkar party for 425 elected seats in the 500-member parliament. The rest of the seats are filled by the military, which does not vote.

Golkar, in power for the last 30 years under President Suharto, is seeking to push its share of the vote to more than 70 percent from the 68 percent it won at the last polls in 1992. The PPP won 17 percent and the PDI 15 percent.
Scores of supporters of Megawati, daughter of Indonesia's first president Sukarno, were seen at the PPP's rallies in Jakarta on Thursday, suggesting an alliance was taking shape.
Megawati has not commented on the move but sources close to her said a decision would be taken soon on PPP efforts to woo her supporters.
"This PPP move is unprecendented. There are going to be meetings to discuss this matter and hopefully 10 days before the elections, there will be a statement issued by Megawati," said one source.
Political observer Mochtar Buchori, who is also an aide of Megawati, said pro-Megawati supporters joined the PPP to express their anger towards the government.

"I tend to see this in a broader context. They (the supporters) need to unite to challenge Golkar...those Megawati supporters are also in need of political vehicles to express their anger," he told Reuters.
Meanwhile, Surjadi said in Dili, the capital of East Timor, that the alliance between Megawati's supporters and those of the PPP was natural and not of major consequence.
